explain.say: First, look at these bars. Each one shows GDP per person: the value of everything a country makes in a year, shared out equally among its people. See how tall the USA bar is, and how small India's is? About 82,000 dollars compared with about 2,500. Which bar surprises you?

Back to the reasons. See geography? Countries with good coasts, rivers and farmland found trade and farming easier, while some hot regions faced diseases like malaria that kept people sick. But tiny Singapore, with almost no land, is very rich. Why do you think a coast helps trade?

faq.q: Why are some countries richer than others?
faq.a: Experts point to many causes: geography, history including colonialism and wars, how fair and stable the rules and government are, education and technology, and trade. They disagree on how much each matters.

Coasts and rivers make trade easier, good soil helps farming, and some tropical areas face diseases like malaria that harm health and work. Geography is not destiny, though: Singapore is tiny with few resources and is very rich.

faq.q: How did colonialism affect countries' wealth?
faq.a: European empires ruled much of the world from the 1500s to the 1900s. Many colonies had resources taken and were set up to benefit the empire, which left weak economies and borders that caused later conflicts. Historians debate how big its lasting effect is.

faq.q: Why do fair rules make countries richer?
faq.a: When laws are fair, contracts are kept, corruption is low and people can keep what they earn, people are more willing to work, invest and start businesses. Acemoglu, Johnson and Robinson won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Economics for research on this.
GDP per person is the value of everything a country produces in a year divided by its number of people. It shows average income, but not how fairly money is shared or how happy people are.
asks: What does GDP per capita mean?

facts: In 2023, GDP per person was roughly 82,000 US dollars in the USA and about 2,500 in India (World Bank, rounded).
Daron Acemoglu, Simon Johnson and James Robinson won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Economics for studying how institutions shape prosperity.
In 1960 South Korea's GDP per person was similar to Ghana's; today it is one of the world's richer economies.

quiz.why: They argue that fair, inclusive laws and institutions let economies grow.
